meta-description: Review and apply schema and data changes between Directus environments.
blocked-nothing-selected: Select at least one collection to migrate
blocked-sequences-unconfirmed: Confirm the sequence reset script first
rollback-confirm-body: Every row this run wrote to {{target}} is removed, and rows it overwrote are restored from the backup. Anything changed on the target since the run finished is lost.
drift-body: This comparison found {{changes}} collection(s) whose schema no longer matches the target. Migrating data now writes onto a schema that has not caught up.
leave-body: The comparison and everything you selected is only held in this tab. Going back to Connect discards it, and nothing already written to the target is undone.
connect-description: URLs and tokens are typed each session and never stored.
connect-fix-unreachable: Check the URL, and check whether you are on the VPN this environment sits behind.
connect-error-timeout: The server did not answer in time
connect-fix-timeout: The host is reachable but slow or blocked. Check the VPN, then try again.
connect-error-not-directus: This is not a Directus API
connect-fix-not-directus: Point the URL at the Directus instance itself, not at a front end or a proxy path.
connect-fix-unauthorised: The token has expired or was mistyped. Generate a new static token in Directus.
connect-fix-forbidden: A migration reads and writes the schema, which only an admin token may do. Ask for a token with admin access.
version-patch-detail: Directus refuses a schema comparison across builds unless it is forced. A patch gap is usually safe, but you are the one saying so.
version-patch-acknowledge: I accept the patch difference and want the comparison forced.
version-major-title: Versions are too far apart — {{source}} vs {{target}}
version-major-detail: Bring both environments to the same minor version before migrating. Forcing this corrupts the target's schema.
version-unknown-detail: One of the versions could not be read, so the gap cannot be judged. Test both connections again.
version-vendor-detail: The two environments run different database engines, and a schema snapshot from one cannot be applied to the other.
relax-pending-title: This target still has relaxed constraints
relax-pending-description: A run loosened NOT NULL, required and UNIQUE on this target and never put them back — the tab was closed or the page reloaded mid-run. Repair before doing anything else.
schema-apply-toggle: Apply schema changes in this run
schema-pick-a-collection: Pick a collection to see what changes inside it.
schema-collection-level-only: The collection itself changes; no individual field does.
schema-field-metadata-only: Directus reports this field as changed, but every difference is internal metadata.
schema-in-sync-detail: Nothing structural to apply. Go straight to data.
data-pick-a-collection: Pick a collection to see its records.
data-pick-a-record: Pick a record to see what changes in it.
data-no-records: Nothing to review in this collection.
data-conflict-note: this record changed on both sides
data-show-audit-records: {{count}} records changed only their audit information — show
data-hide-audit-records: {{count}} records changed only their audit information — hide
data-in-sync-detail_one: {{count}} collection compared, and every record is identical on both sides. There is nothing to migrate.
data-in-sync-detail_other: All {{count}} collections compared, and every record is identical on both sides. There is nothing to migrate.
apply-order-backup: Capture a backup of the target
apply-order-mirror: Delete rows the source does not have
apply-destructive-warning_one: {{count}} change removes data and cannot be undone automatically.
apply-destructive-warning_other: {{count}} changes remove data and cannot be undone automatically.
apply-backup-mandatory: A backup of the target is captured first. This cannot be turned off.
apply-reviewed: I have reviewed every change above.
apply-confirm-body: {{records}} records will be written and {{deletes}} destructive changes applied. This cannot be undone automatically.
run-sequence-detail: Migrated ids do not advance the database sequence, so the next record the CMS creates would collide. Run this against the target database.
data-sequence-title: Reset these sequences on the target first
data-sequence-detail: Run this on the target database before migrating. Note: migrated rows carry their source ids, so the sequences will need running again after the run finishes — copy the script below and run it manually.
data-sequence-confirm: I have run this script on the target database.
data-mirror-title: Mirror data: delete {{count}} rows the source does not have
data-mirror-detail: Runs after every row has been written, on the selected collections only. The rows are in the backup, so a rollback brings them back — but nothing else will.
data-delete-only-disabled: Only rows the target has and the source does not. Turn on "mirror data" to remove them.
data-open-value: Double-click to see the full value
